title: How I built a full boss event for my mobile game with AI – art, voices, music and cutscenes (and where it went wrong)
author: thexyba
selftext:
>I’m a solo dev building **Scitch**, a live multiplayer reaction game for up to 24 players. Today our first boss event went live: **“Return of the Eye”** – a solo mission with 4 chapters, 3 lives, and a boss that heals itself if you’re too slow.  
>  
>Here’s how the AI parts came together:  
>  
>**Art – Gemini image models**  
Backgrounds, the boss and the event art. The key was always passing reference images, otherwise every new image drifted into a slightly different style.  
>  
>**Voices – Gemini TTS + speech-to-text check**  
Every cutscene line exists in German and English. Each line gets transcribed back with speech-to-text to catch mispronunciations. That turned out to be necessary: in German, the word for “pairs” kept coming out sounding like “pause”.  
>  
>**Music – Google Lyria**  
Spooky tracks for the trailer and shorts.  
>  
>**Cutscenes and trailers – code**  
Every video is HTML/JS, rendered frame by frame with Playwright and encoded with ffmpeg. It means I can change a line of text and re-render instead of re-editing a video.  
>  
>**Game logic – Claude Code**  
The Go game server runs the boss fight: 4,000 HP, healing 2.5 % per second when you stop hitting it. Balancing was the part where AI helped the least – that needed lots of play-testing.  
>  
>**What I’d do differently:** automate the quality checks earlier. Most of my time went into catching small things like overlapping text in videos or a voice line cut off at the end.  
>  
>Happy to answer questions about the pipeline. If you want to try the boss yourself, there’s a free beta for iPhone & Android.
